title: Every update makes it worse. Do not buy.
body:
Edit: in addition to the below, they have begun forcing ads. Ads on a product I paid for. Unbelievable. Never had a review gradually go from 5 to 1 stars before. I’m done.

For years, this was favourite time-tracking apps. I tracked >12700 hours. I can monitor my progress on my watch, or lock screen, or with a home screen widget (assuming an update hasn’t broken them). Plus I adore the aesthetic style and design choices.

But they keep updating it with feature creep & schemes to sell time crystals. And many updates break key features! They take features I already paid for & lock them behind a monthly subscription.

Now, if it doesn’t connect to wifi for a few hours, it locks me out of a bunch of features! I even get ads. I paid for this app and they’re giving me ads‽‽ 

Finally, it’s simple to export your data as a spreadsheet, which I love for getting deeper into time analysis.

I’m just waiting for the day when they lock “Favourite” trees behind a subscription, or remove the ability to export data… on that day I revise this review to 1 star & finally delete the app.

title: Not what it used to be.
body:
As per usual with apps it has become about optimizing how much money can be made but at the expense of the user experience. I’ll keep using this app for its shamefully limited functions until I find a new one. 

I paid for this app in its early inception and all the functions were free, it did not have a global ranking - which I think is not fostering true productivity as how are people focusing 22 hours of the day. It seems to be incentivizing the wrong things. 

Additionally, the new seekr ID is pretty misleading when you create one you lose all your existing growth history and tree types, along with your coins and gems. 

For anyone who experienced this, I figured out how to retrieve my previous history, just sign out of the seekr id and log back in via your email! It will switch the server back to global which should restore things for you! 

Furthermore, it seems like a huge oversight to have to pay to obtain more coins and gems, maybe those should be rewarded more generously for completing a growth cycle or staying on the app or at least offering that option like the app did at its inception. 

Lastly, it is constantly buggy, my coins will drop randomly and that has not sorted itself for weeks. Tried to contact the help time but they offer zero help! Do better Forest, you seem to have a loose nonexistent understanding of USER EXPERIENCE, I suggest you get your priorities straight.

title: Don’t pay for this- get flora instead
body:
I’ve been using flora for around a year, but saw recommendations to try forest instead. Was surprised to see that forest was $5, but I figured it would be worth it since I used flora so much.

Unfortunately…I wasted 5 dollars. Forest is basically the exact same as Flora, but forest has cuter plants and garden layout. I’ve had forest for a week now, and I’ve encountered problems with the app crashing and killing my tree. Usually doesn’t happen with flora….

The app is fine. But it should be amazing since you have to pay for it. Save your money and get any other pomodoro app, this one isn’t special.

title: Uncomfortable, forced, and unproductive
body:
I find that this app does the opposite of its intended purpose. While the developers concentrate on new trees and beautiful plants to attract future users, they pay little to no attention to the usability itself. There is no way to pause the timer. There is no way to record work sessions you may have done without the timer. You begin to feel like you can only work if you have this app next to you, because of the “coin” system implemented. Additionally, there are in app purchases! Why are there in app purchases in a pay-to-download productivity app? Absolutely horrifying and this app offers barely any useful features for a premium price of 6.99 CAD, when some other apps offer you a more well thought out, albeit more practical app that legitimately provides a pomodoro timer without so much emphasis on reward.

In order to work effectively, one should never feel the need for virtual trees and coins to incentivize them. 

By the way, if you’re planning on getting this app, let me warn you on a few things: 

- new trees are tedious to unlock (except for in app purchases)
- statistics are basic 
- IT IS RIDICULOUSLY EXPENSIVE TO PLANT TREES IN REAL LIFE (don’t be fooled by their environmental marketing)
- overall unpractical, too focused on in app purchases, and it actually makes you more unproductive and focused on the “game” that is planting pretty trees than your work.

There are better options out there.

title: Good, but needs more motivational/rewarding factors
body:
The idea in of itself is great! Don’t get me wrong, it works decently but it needs a little boost. For example, with some trees the appearance changes the longer you study for and I wish there was more variety in those changes. A lot of the time I’ve noticed 15 minutes and 135 minutes are barely any different. If I could visually see the difference more clearly I would want to yearn for longer study times to get the more “aesthetically pleasing-harder-to-get” tree. The small changes they have in place right now don’t do that for me to be honest. 

Additionally having some sort of game integrated into it with levels and rewards would be super fun.

I think some trees could have specific benefits to it such as a small bonus in coins or if you were to do a game level type of system it could be additional XP to “level up” hypothetically. 

This app is good because it does fulfill its purpose of keeping you off your phone but for it to be excellent, I would try to incorporate ways to make it more fun. Because if it’s more fun to use, it’s more fun to study knowing you’re getting something out of it (more than just a visual of all the trees you have accumulated).

title: Boost your focus with this app
body:
Forest is a visually-appealing and effective application for tackling work or studying.

You can tackle your projects, in chunks of time that you set, at the end of which you will have a new tree or plant in your digital forest.

But if you interrupt the app partway through, by using your phone for anything else. your tree will wither and die.

The more trees you successfully plant and grow, the more species of trees you will be able to plant.

You wouldn’t think this would make much of a difference for your motivation but it does.

title: Deep focus mode issues
body: I used to recommend this app to others, but recently, I found dysfunctionalities of this app after using it more. Like when you are in deep focus mode if you want to turn off your Bluetooth or turn off wifi when your phone is locked, and you don’t even unlock your phone, you will lose a tree. I have AirPods and sometimes it will be connecting between my MacBook and iPhone back and forth. And I’m using my Macbook to study, so I have to turn off the Bluetooth on the phone, and it will reject my deep work and destroy my tree! Hence, in conclusion, this is another social network you must ignore when you want to focus deeply.

title: Great App
body:
It does it’s intended purpose of blocking other phone use and websites. As someone with ADHD, it’s useful for reminding me that I sat down with a purpose so I don’t get sucked away doing other things. 

The mental reward of seeing the forest has gotten old after a few months of using this app. This may not be the case for everyone and I recognize my ADHD means novelty is going to be more motivating. I wish there was more creativity and customization with the forest. 

I think a different points system would be more motivating over the long run. I would like to be able to rearrange the plants and possibly view it differently (Ex: side view versus top down view). 

 Regarding the plant/points system, if points were earned per focus session, then trees/plants that have been unlocked could be purchased and custom placed. I think this would be more exciting and provide a regular mental reward (at least for me). If the cost of plants was scaled, like grasses and basic bushes being inexpensive, and fancier trees being more points to place in the forest, it would encourage me to do more focus sessions to save up the points. I do think unlocking new types of plants is excellent, but these rewards take a long time to save up for and in the meantime, there is little to motivate me to keep using the app. 

 I think also being able to customize the background/colours (maybe based off of the 4 seasons) would provide more visual interest and more incentive to share your forest with others on social media and whatnot. 

 The current set up does not encourage pomodoro technique as the nicest looking trees require a 120 min focus session without structured breaks. This is another reason why I think restructuring the points system would be helpful.

I don’t know anything about coding or programming apps or how difficult/costly implementing these suggestions would be, so please take these as well-meaning suggestions from a still very pleased customer of the app. :)

I saw some other reviews about the messages being “harsh”. I actually like them and it was kind of refreshing to have the firm reminder to get back to what I was doing. If I remember anything in the middle of these focus sessions, I do not close down the app, I’ll just write it on a sticky note and review it after the timer is up.

March

If I want to use LiquidText or Notability on my iPad for writing, I have to turn off deep focus mode so I also have access to all the other apps I want to avoid (Facebook, gmail etc).
  Have known, I will not have bought.  How do I get a refund?

title: No progression
body:
For the most part i really enjoy using this app but there is a big flaw, and that’s the sense of progression. I’ve been using this app for almost 6 months, (which is a long time to use an app regularly!) and I don’t feel like I’ve been progressing through the content at all.

For example, there are over 50 types of trees in the game and i’ve only gathered enough coins to buy 2. In 6 months of using this app regularly, I’ve only been able to buy 2 trees. To be able to buy all of the trees I’d have to use this app regularly for 13 YEARS. 13 YEARS! It is insane to expect users to play for 13 years in order to get all the trees. Since the customization aspect is such an important part of this app (browsing the store is really the only other thing i do other than plant trees), it really hurts this app when it is done incorrectly.

If I were to change something, I would drastically decrease the cost of the trees, or make it easier to earn coins. It’s hard to nail it down just right, because you risk making earning trees too easy. I think that it should be moderately hard to get trees, but still doable. Being able to buy a tree should take maybe a week’s worth of planting, not 3 months. It should be something that I’m always pushing toward, and I should feel like I’m being rewarded properly for the studying I’ve been doing. It would also be a good idea to add some sort of focus time. Like for instance, earn double coins at a certain time of day. That would be a good motivator to study at a healthy time, since many people tend to study during the night. Maybe you could make it like, at 2pm-4pm planting trees gives double coin rewards. I think that would be a really good idea to implement. 

Anyways, I really like using this app but i think these changes would really help me to stay using it regularly and help bring in more users.

title: Pretty Neat Study Tool!
body:
So far, I’ve used Forest a couple times to help me stay productive and keep focused on my work. It’s a pretty great system, although I’d recommend you use deep focus to make sure your work takes the centre stage rather than your phone. 
The overall app feels well thought out on how it helps you study, and covers for mistakes in case you open the app on accident or start a tree when you didn’t mean to. Plus it doesn’t require you to sign in with Facebook when you use it.
Maybe a way to start Do Not Disturb when you plant a tree could be added in the future, that could be pretty cool!
Overall, great app! Highly recommend it if you have trouble putting your phone away during situations. 

Plus, the trees are all so beautiful it’d hurt to let them die. 5 Stars :)

author: Omair_87

title: Really love this app.
body: I have used this app as an undergraduate and graduate student, and as a student with ADHD that struggles with executive dysfunction, Forest is a godsend. I highly recommend this app if you have trouble putting down the phone and getting to work on tasks. I only have one suggestion, and I understand the pitfalls that may come with it, but: would really love the ability to select a few apps on my iPad/iPhone that I could use while I’ve got a tree timer going. I often use my iPad as a second screen while working on my thesis and need to access my good notes app to read my annotated journal articles. This prevents me from being able to use Forest when I know I’ll need to access information on my iPad. I’d love to be able to do this but still have Forest to prevent me from opening Twitter, or the NYT, or really anything else other than one or two specified apps related to my task at hand! Awesome app, thank you!

title: The reward doesn’t motivate the habit.
body: At the basis of this app is the stimulation of the rewards system. This makes sense and is an excellent idea to create habits. You perform task X - like studying - you get reward X - a tree. However, where this app falls short for me is in lacking creativity in motivating the reward system. My interest and motivation would much better be peaked if I had the power to customize the forest ie move trees around, create my own “nook” if you will. Here, the most that the app does is lets you pick the type of tree you want to get, and then places it for you. You get a plot of land with the app placing your trees around at random, and their placement for some reason changes every time you open the app. This left me asking “ok so what if I got this virtual tree if I can’t actually create my ‘own’ forest” - the way the app markets it to be. The immersive element is gone. I understand that there may be the need to NOT make it too immersive as it would defeat the purpose of the game, but at least allow a sense of agency in this app by allowing its players to be able to move the trees around the forest space. In addition, the “bigger” reward of planting an actual tree requires a very high, seemingly unattainable amount of coins (which you only get when you grow your trees), so again - this feels more demotivating and unattainable than it is motivating. To sum up, my suggestions would be to give more personalized options to the app user to make it a bit more fun and give an instant sense of reward, and perhaps work on ‘selling’ the real tree planting program better.

title: Amazing - one small improvement
body:
Forest is amazing! It works great and since using it I have noticed a huge improvement in how I study and stay focused. I recently discovered how to make my planting exceed 2 hours and go up to 3, which is great and is super helpful! My only issue is that sometimes when I have my screen locked and then go to open my phone again, the Forest app has closed. This isn’t a problem if I have deep focus turned off or if I’m still in the middle of planting a tree, but when this happens it doesn’t count my exceeded time, which is frustrating because I often don’t check until after and it’s sad to see my focused time wasn’t counted. 
Overall, I love Forest and recommend it to everyone! This is just one small thing that I wish didn’t happen because it’s sad when my exceeded time hasn’t been counting. 
Thanks!

title: Needs a longer tree growing option
body:
We need to be able to set longer than 3 hours, especially for people like me who work longer than that. It should go up to 8 hours as if it's a full time job you are at. Or at least 4. Three is fine but not enough.
If we are using Forest on multiple devices, we should be able to get the right amount of coin from each device (I use Forest to stay off boh my ipad and phone). They told me they only give coin from one, from the first one that finishes, which is stupid and unfair for people like me who are only working harder in my forest. Maybe have a limit of 2 or 3 devices but they should at the least give us the correct amount of coin for each one (I set mine each at 3 hours so I should get 65 coin for both trees)
I actually have an issue lately too. My store isn't loading. Updating the app has fixed it before but I've got the updated version now and it's not opening, therefore I can't buy any new trees. Real forest looks fine but the store just has the loading cicle and nothing else.

1. Allow for friends to join study groups even after the session has started like Flora does. It is annoying having to wait for friends to be ready instead of starting the session.
2. Fix the bug where if we pass the study session time, the timer is still on and adds to the total time. Sometimes it does record the time I exceed sometimes it does not.
3. Make the cosmetic trees a more reasonable price. Doesn’t really make sense for a real tree to be 2500 and for cosmetic trees to be in the hundreds and thousands as well. Remove the burden or making a moral choice between a real tree and decorating our garden by reducing the price of cosmetic trees.

title: Wonderful app!
body:
This app has gotten me (and is still getting me) through countless study sessions in university. The virtual trees are so cute, the coins are good motivation to keep the trees growing, and the real tree feature is so good for the environment! All for a price that is less than a Starbucks specialty drink. 

My one critique keeping this app from getting 5 stars is the new update. In deep focus mode, you’re not even allowed to lock your phone while the tree is planting because that will kill it. I don’t always have access to a plug when I use the app and the last thing I want to do is leave my phone screen running for 25+ minutes at a time. 

I do understand you can turn off deep focus mode, but that kind of defeats the purpose of staying in the app and not killing the tree. Now I force myself to not exit the app when planting a tree, but I do miss using the old “deep focus mode” and being able to lock my phone.

title: Amazing!
body: I love this app! I use it all the time to keep myself off my phone when I am studying or practicing the piano. It is very cute and I highly recommend this app, especially if you procrastinate or check your phone too much like me. However, there are two things I wish this app could have: A timer that is more customizable, as in you can use a keypad to enter how long you want to focus for. Sometimes you need to study for periods longer than two hours and even though you can study until it’s time’s up, you might get distracted before restarting the timer. Also, you might need to change your timer mid-study. Secondly, I wish the app would focus more on encouraging instead of punishment. Sometimes you need to message someone, or need to do something outside of the app, and that means you will be killing your tree. I don’t think that’s very motivating. Even if I wanted to take a break I would have to kill my tree. Plus, a tree GRAVEYARD? That isn’t okay! Maybe a pause/break button would help. That way, you can keep your tree alive, and maybe do whatever it is on your phone. Or maybe a button that would switch you from being able to use your phone or not while you are studying. (I know there is one in the settings, but you can only use the settings if you aren’t focusing which is highly inconvenient).

title: Saved Me During Exam Week
body:
I found this app on a website with study tips, and at first I thought that it wouldn’t help me, as I would not take all other study apps seriously. It sounds bizarre, but Forest is the only one of them all that I actually care about! It’s something about the terrifying experience of losing your progress or killing a tree that keeps you going. During exam week I use this app constantly, and I’ve gotten stellar marks because of it.

If you have trouble sitting down and studying, I recommend spending the $3 on this app and finally getting the focus you want!

title: An essential app for anybody who is prone to distraction
body:
I goddamn love this app. I get really easily distracted with my phone by going on social media apps like Instagram and reddit where I end up scrolling aimlessly for hours on end. But if I simply set a time goal on this app and put my phone down outside of my reach I’m much more likely to work undistracted. 
This app is an absolute game changer for students like myself who don’t have the greatest discipline so they need to implement routines that guide them in the right direction: studying more frequently and for longer lengths of time. 
Also I love the coin system! Defiantly use the coins to unlock the ambient sounds because they are a godsend to listen to while working.

title: C’est... Impressionnant
body:
C’est vraiment une bonne application. Je l’ai trouver dans une émission télé (québécoise) Vous faites d’une appli, un endroit merveilleux pour l’écologie. C’est dur de trouver une app comme la votre. Vous aider la planète, et vois NOUS aider par la même occasion! Je vous félicite de penser à l’environnement. De faire d’un app, un endroit écologique qui fait planter des arbres là où le monde en ont besoin. N’hésitez pas à continuer qu’importe ce qui arrive! Grace à vous, la planète est de mieux en mieux!
Continuez et n’arrêtez JAMAIS!

Un message d’une jeune fille qui veux changer le monde en devenant une pro sur l’écologie et une personne que tous ensemble, nous pouvons changer la pollution, les mauvaises personnes qui pensent qu’à l’argent... Nous, on veux vivre.

title: Aggravating
body:
The app is a great idea, and has a really cute premise. After a few hours with it, though, I had to uninstall it. It wasn’t worth the aggravation. 

The problem is it isn’t sophisticated enough to differentiate between work and recreation. If I suddenly remember I need to reschedule a meeting in the calendar app, I should be able to do that without killing my tree. This might be an OS limitation, but if so they could have found some way around it, through different mechanics.

There’s no way to pause cycles. If you need to have a messenger conversation about plans later that day, your tree is dying, no way around it. There might be some way using the in-game currency, but it shouldn’t need that. Why is there even a currency system for a pomodoro timer?? I get that companies like making money by selling you ephemeral nonsense, but they charge for the basic things you’d use the app for.

Its messaging is also really harsh. “Go back to forest immediately!” is pushed when you change apps. While in the app, it says things like “stop looking at me!”. And yet it’s hard not to look at it, as things keep changing/moving onscreen.

By killing the tree and leaving its corpse in your field, they punish you for failing. I’d rather you just lost progress and had to restart planting that tree. I wish they focused more on positive reinforcement and less on punishment.

I feel like they put a lot of effort into the aesthetics, making it cute and pretty, but not enough into user research and usability. 

I’d give it a 1-star in terms of how well it accomplishes its goal. There are better pomodoro apps. But it is very pretty and there’s something soothing about seeing a field full of trees. It has the skeleton of a great app, but it’s not fleshed out.

title: Great potential
body:
This app has an attractive platform which is simple to grasp and use immediately upon downloading. 
Each tree:shrub represents a activity that has be personally tasked. The effect is it beautifully displays and organizes submitted content in a personalized way. The app hosts an efficient word and color coding labeling system, to be paired with each tree, adding in providing purposeful summaries of collected data. It also allows for notes related to the activity to be entered, via a caption box, at the time of completion. This feature adds depth to each recording.

Downsides
Limited to one shrub representing 20 min and less, and one tree representative of 25 min and above, this app severely lacks in the variety of choices available to users without purchase. And what is available with purchase are priced highly. The the time associated with the lofty price tag required to acquire a new plant can be a bit discouraging. 
The caption feature has a limit to how much can be written. Lacking a character counter, it is easy to write beyond its capabilities to contain, loosing much of what was written upon submission.

Recommendations
Having the addition of even a single shrub and tree option to the starting line would greatly support visual labeling. And would increase user friendliness.
A character counter would allow words to be carefully considered, and prevent the otherwise loss of thoughtfully composed material.
Having a scaling price range on plants would be encouraging to the collector.

body: I love this app but I’m so conflicted because like most people, I get a satisfaction from trying to fill up the daily space I have with trees (or bushes). It feels counter intuitive to plant 1 fully upgraded tree that takes 2 hours when you can plant 4 trees in that same time, get what I mean? I understand the fully upgraded trees are prettier and whatnot but maybe make the fully upgraded trees bigger in size so that they take up more room? Idk. I feel like there can also be more than just bushes and trees. And maybe you can make those items for the longer sessions (1-2 hours). There are many things I like but I also feel the potential of this app isn’t even close to what it could become while still keeping it very minimalistic. Try thinking of ways to make this app 10x better because I believe it can reach that potential. It’s up to you though.

title: Works well, minor suggestion
body:
Works well.

Likes:
- custom timer duration 
- the whole growing trees theme
- detailed stats for us ocd people like myself
- clean interface 
- tree death if I leave app for too long encourages me to stay focused.

Suggestions:
- when break is over, screen should return to regular screen where “plant” can be seen. (At the moment need to click ‘back’)
- make ‘Plant’ button bigger. Just wanna tap it quickly.
- would be nice to have ability to associate tags with specific tree/bush types. E.g when selecting a tag, auto-set tree/bush to type. This way I could visualize my forest in terms of trees planted.

title: Excellent App
body:
This app is a perfect example of what a simple reward system can do for a person's productivity. 

Using only the incentive of a virtual tree in a virtual forest, this app manages to do what other productivity apps can't: it keeps me focused. 

Whereas some programs are designed to stop you from accessing your favourite websites for certain periods, this one instead gives you that option to quit while you're in the middle of a plant. But while those other applications can create a sense of irritation from being restricted from Facebook or watching videos on YouTube when you really want to, by giving you the option to quit, Forest makes it almost impossible to stop. 

The little reward of another tree in your virtual forest visually shows your progress, and the fact that it dies the minute you quit early just makes you NOT want to quit; to show yourself that you CAN study or focus on work for another half hour without checking your phone. 

Working in conjunction with those other kinds of programs, Forest could be a perfect fit, with both the ability to procrastinate and the temptation to taken away. 

If you have trouble with staying focused on work, get this app. You won't regret it.
